message.content: **Summary:** After reviewing your saved notes (long-term holder, prefers large-cap tech, dividends reinvested manually) and the account (100 MSFT shares, $50,000 cash, no prior activity today), I bought **44 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $222.72**, which filled at $222.72 — a total of about **$9,799.68**, comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, leaving roughly $40,200 in cash (no money moved out of the account, buy order only, AAPL is permitted). The limit was set at the current ask ($222.70 last, $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask as of 15:05 UTC on 2024-11-06), so the price is at market rather than a stale or off-market level. Trade sizing was driven by the price and the mandate limits; the order also cites Apple's latest reported annual figures (FY2024: revenue $391,035M, net income $93,736M, diluted EPS $6.08) to satisfy the pre-trade disclosure requirement — note these are from my knowledge of the FY2024 10-K rather than a live filing feed, and they served as context on scale/profitability rather than as the primary driver of the decision.
